whatItShows.title: What it shows
items: Each **row** is a world-fact the story keeps talking about (a rule, a piece of backstory, an object's history) — found by the analysis, not authored.
Read a row **left-to-right**: it's that fact's **revelation pacing** — when it enters the story and how it's fed to the reader over the scenes.

rows.Debut — soft shade: the fact’s FIRST reveal — where it enters the story
rows.Support — solid dot: a later reveal that adds to / repeats the fact
rows.Paradox — red ◆: a reveal that contradicts earlier canon
rows.a line across a row: the fact’s span, first→last reveal: long = WOVEN, short = DUMPED
rows.debut far right: the fact is introduced LATE — check it’s set up before it matters
rows.columns: scenes in reading order; the bands group them by act/chapter

rows.Paradox: facts that contradict themselves — fix these first
rows.No page: the fact recurs but you never wrote a lore page for it — "canon by accident"
rows.Has page: facts you’ve written an authored lore page for

decisions.title: Decisions it guides
items: **Fix contradictions** — a Paradox marker means two reveals disagree; open the topic to see them (the deeper cross-scene check lives in Coherence).
**Seed earlier** — if a fact debuts late but is leaned on early, plant it sooner.
**Write it down** — a recurring "No page" fact is canon by accident; open it and formalize it into a lore page.
